history.dynasty: Yadava of Devagiri (13th century, Hemadpanthi); renovated by Rani Ahilyabai Holkar (inscription records 1706); Peshwa-era care
history.summary: Parli Vaijnath is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, set in a fortified stone temple complex atop a ~75-80 ft hill near Mount Meru at Parli in Beed district. Tradition holds it was built in the 13th century under the Yadavas of Devagiri by their chief minister Hemadpant (Hemadri/Karanadip Hemadri), fell into ruin, and was reconstructed in 1706 by Rani Ahilyabai Holkar of the Marathas (the temple bears Sanskrit inscriptions; Peshwas later maintained it); some strands credit the original shrine to Yudhishthira of the Mahabharata (verify). Legend says Ravana, granted the Jyotirlinga by Shiva to carry to Lanka on condition it never touch the ground, was tricked into setting it down at Parli, fixing it there forever. 'Vaijnath'/'Vaidyanath' means 'Lord of Physicians' - Shiva is believed to have descended as a divine healer (associated with the Amrit/Dhanavantari legend and the Bhasmasura-Mohini episode), so devotees are permitted to touch the linga for healing. Rare custom: Tulsi is offered to Shiva and Bilva to Vishnu here, the reverse of usual practice, symbolising Shaiva-Vaishnava unity; unusually for a Jyotirlinga, both Shiva and Parvati are enshrined together ('Unique Kashi'). NOTE - Jyotirlinga identity: some traditions and texts place the Vaidyanath Jyotirlinga at Deoghar (Jharkhand) instead of Parli; the identity is disputed between the two sites (verify before asserting).

name: Shri Vaijnath (Vaidyanath) Jyotirlinga Temple
town_description: Parli (Parli Vaijnath) is a pilgrim town in Beed district of Maharashtra's Marathwada region, known almost entirely for its Jyotirlinga shrine; it is also an industrial town with a well-known thermal power plant and a cotton market. The temple sits on a hill above the town at the confluence of the Brahma, Venu and Saraswati rivers (Triveni). It is commonly paired with the Yogeshwari Devi temple at Ambajogai, ~25 km away, in pilgrimage circuits.

travel.airport: Nanded Airport, ~91-114 km (limited connectivity; verify). Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) Airport, ~200-225 km (better connectivity; verify).
travel.railway: Parli Vaijnath railway station serves the town; sources conflict on whether it is in town or ~24 km away (CONFLICT - verify). Trains run from Nanded, Parbhani and Hyderabad directions.
travel.road: Well connected by MSRTC and private buses to Nanded, Latur, Beed, Jalna and Hingoli; Ambajogai ~25 km by road. Local autos within Parli.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; Mahashivratri and the Shravan month are the most vibrant but most crowded.
